title: Analysis of serum haptoglobin fucosylation in hepatocellular carcinoma and liver cirrhosis of different etiologies.

screening.reason: The abstract reports a specific glycan modification (bifucosylated tetra‑antennary glycan on haptoglobin) that differs between HCC and cirrhosis patients, indicating a potential biomarker. However, performance metrics (e.g., AUC, sensitivity, specificity) are not provided, so the full text is needed for quantitative assessment.

title: Asymptomatic phosphomannose isomerase deficiency (MPI-CDG) initially mistaken for excessive alcohol consumption.

screening.reason: The abstract reports a clear glycan biomarker (carbohydrate‑deficient transferrin) that is elevated in patients with asymptomatic phosphomannose isomerase deficiency, linking a glycan feature to a disease state with quantitative CDT levels.

entities.evidence_sentence: The test result (~17% disialotransferrin, reference interval <2.0%; ~3% asialotransferrin, reference 0%) was confirmed by analysis of a second sample, while another alcohol biomarker, phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in whole-blood, was negative.

The test result (~17% disialotransferrin, reference interval <2.0%; ~3% asialotransferrin, reference 0%) was confirmed by analysis of a second sample, while another alcohol biomarker, phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in whole-blood, was negative.
The abnormal 'type-1' transferrin glycoform pattern indicated a defect in N-glycan assembly occurring in congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG), a family of rare inherited metabolic disorders.

evidence_sentences.sentence: In a routine company health check-up, a 32-year-old woman presented a highly elevated serum level of carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (CDT), a biomarker for excessive alcohol consumption.

The test result (~17% disialotransferrin, reference interval <2.0%; ~3% asialotransferrin, reference 0%) was confirmed by analysis of a second sample, while another alcohol biomarker, phosphatidylethanol (PEth) in whole-blood, was negative.

Probing for the underlying enzyme defect(s) using cultured skin fibroblasts demonstrated normal activity of phosphomannomutase, whereas the activity of phosphomannose isomerase (MPI) was reduced (0.64 mU/mg protein, reference 2.1-6.9), pointing to CDG of the MPI subtype (formerly called CDG-Ib).

relations.normalization_note: The glycan term "disialotransferrin" includes the protein transferrin; the glycan component is a disialylated N‑glycan. The evidence supports an increased level of this glycoform in MPI‑CDG, so only the glycan name needs normalization.

title: Abundance-ratio-based semiquantitative analysis of site-specific N-linked glycopeptides present in the plasma of hepatocellular carcinoma patients.

screening.reason: The study links specific site‑specific N‑linked glycoforms of vitronectin in plasma to hepatocellular carcinoma, reporting a significant increase in the fucosyl/non‑fucosyl ratio in HCC versus normal plasma. However, the abstract lacks quantitative metrics (fold change, p‑value, sample size) and detailed performance data, so the full text is needed.

title: Glycation of the complement regulatory protein CD59 is a novel biomarker for glucose handling in humans.

screening.reason: The study reports a glycated form of CD59 (GCD59) as a circulating biomarker that correlates quantitatively with HbA1c, predicts 2‑hour OGTT glucose, and decreases with intensified insulin therapy in humans.
